exposure: Implementation of European Working Time Directive (EWTD)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 18,761 nulliparous, term, singleton, vertex presentation, spontaneously labouring women (Robson Group 1) delivering in a tertiary referral center between 2008 and 2017.
finding: The study found an association between obstetric trainee working practices (specifically nocturnal hours and EWTD implementation) and increased Caesarean Section rates, as well as reduced Operative Vaginal Delivery rates in Robson Group 1 women.
mod_finding: CS rates were higher at nighttime and significantly increased post-EWTD, while operative vaginal delivery rates significantly decreased post-EWTD.
